questions.question: Which fruit has the most?
questions.explain: Count the symbols in each row. Grapes has 6, the most. Bananas has only 2, the fewest — easy to mix up.

questions.question: Which pet has the fewest?
questions.explain: Find the row with the least symbols. Birds has 3, the fewest. Cats has 8, the most — don't pick the biggest row.

questions.question: How many more kids chose soccer than swimming?
questions.explain: Subtract the smaller from the bigger: 7 minus 4 is 3. Do not add them (11) or just give the bigger number (7).

questions.question: How many balls are there altogether?
questions.explain: Add both rows: 5 plus 3 is 8. Giving just one row (5 or 3) misses the other colour.

questions.question: Maya collected leaves from four trees. Which tree gave her the most leaves?
questions.explain: Count each row. Oak has 8, the most. Birch has only 3, the fewest — easy to mix up.

questions.question: Leo has more crayons than pencils. How many more crayons does he have?
questions.explain: Take the smaller from the bigger: 9 minus 6 is 3. Adding (15) or just naming the bigger number (9) is not the difference.

visual.caption: What is in Leo's pencil case

questions.question: The class is selling treats. How many treats are there in all?
questions.explain: Add all three rows: 7 plus 4 plus 5 is 16. Giving just one row (7 or 5) forgets the others.

questions.question: Tom is picking a marble. Which colour has the fewest? He wants the rarest one.
questions.explain: Find the shortest row. Yellow has 3, the fewest. Red has 8, the most — don't grab the biggest row.

questions.question: Dad plants 2 more white flowers. Now, how many more red flowers are there than white flowers?
questions.explain: First add 2 to white: 5 plus 2 is 7. Then subtract: 8 minus 7 is 1. Forgetting to add the 2 gives 3.

questions.question: Ben says: I have 9 stars and 5 moons, so I have 14 more stars than moons. What did he do wrong?
questions.explain: To find how many more, subtract: 9 minus 5 is 4, not 14. Ben added to get the total instead of the difference.

questions.question: You give away 2 blue popsicles. How many popsicles are there now in all?
questions.explain: Add all rows first: 6 plus 4 plus 8 is 18. Then take away 2: 18 minus 2 is 16. Giving just the blue row (4) forgets the others.

questions.question: How many more girls than boys are in the class?
questions.explain: Subtract: 12 minus 7 is 5. Adding (19) or naming the bigger number (12) does not give the difference.
